adaptations.RTS-04-11: Ready inventory is Alert+5. A dispatch takes at least300s from the order; the launch lane also runs its printed sequence. The first completion is max(Alert+5, lane sequence); subsequent aircraft use separate lanes, not an instant multi-plane spawn.
adaptations.RTS-04-12: Queues reserve inventory immediately. A disabled deck aborts its active sequence and restarts the full sequence when operational. Cancelling returns reserved aircraft, without counting a sortie. Physical parked/respot locations are not yet implemented.
adaptations.RTS-04-13: A valid Low-altitude quarter-FMP touchdown inside the existing1.5nm approach gate reserves the recovery lane for60s, or a vertical spot for180s. The first touchdown is immediate when eligible, and subsequent ones respect throughput. The1.5nm gate is an RTS approach abstraction, not a source sensor or runway range. Ship-heading alignment uses1degree procedural tolerance.
adaptations.RTS-04-14: On recovery, source fuel/arm work precedes alert work. Ship servicing has12 simultaneous places; individual jobs occupy a place for their complete fuel/arm stage. Aircraft are homogeneous class inventory; individual airframe damage and cumulative daily sortie identity remain unimplemented.
adaptations.RTS-05-11: One-second clocks replace30s increments without shortening source delays. Detection timers reset when a target leaves the eligible envelope. Negative reaction adjustments do not grant invented over-range contacts; that predictive branch remains unimplemented.
adaptations.RTS-05-12: Flight radar arcs use actual heading and altitude bands. Groups require explicit group metadata and are not inferred from accidental proximity. This first version does not implement the source group-signature uplift.
adaptations.RTS-08-11: Use the explicit instruction in8.1.5 to roll for each missile intercepted in the Point Defense band. Log actual time-to-go; do not replace the printed table with a distance interpolation. Gun caliber comes from the fitted platform binding, not its generic weapon alias.

limitations: Full SAM intercept shot tables and ATA resolution remain separate unimplemented branches.
Unknown platform size, radar fit, sea/wind conditions, launch spots, or armor metadata must not be guessed.
Current source aircraft signatures lack full aspect and loadout overrides; strict radar therefore requires an explicit verified signature when such a branch matters.
Runway throughput, aircraft deck parking/respot, individual daily sorties, refuelling, and complete land/air sensor classes remain outstanding.
